> Significant changes — new constitutive models, solver algorithms, audit or
> regulatory features — require the RFC process. **Discuss in this issue
> first.** A maintainer commits the RFC file to `rfcs/NNNN-short-name.md` once
> the design is agreed, and the status is set to `Accepted`, `Deferred` or
> `Rejected`. This project does not accept external pull requests — see
> [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Summary

One-paragraph explanation.

## Motivation

Why is this needed? What workflow or standard does it serve? Who is the
question of interest, and what are its model risk and model influence under
ASME V&V 40?

## Detailed design

The proposed design in detail: data models, algorithms, APIs, numerics,
verification strategy.

## Verification strategy

How will this be verified, and against what reference? Name the analytical
solution, published correlation, or standard. A numerical model with no stated
verification reference will not be accepted.

## Drawbacks / alternatives

Why not do it another way? What did you reject, and why?

## Unresolved questions

Open items to settle before acceptance.
